title: Prediction of the infecting organism in peritoneal dialysis patients with acute peritonitis using interpretable Tsetlin Machines
new_feature: Applies multiclass TMs (pyTsetlinMachineParallel) in a hierarchical binary scheme to predict the infecting organism from peritoneal-effluent immune biomarkers, with clause stencil visualisation, feature ranking for biomarker minimisation and precision-based clause pruning.

datasets.input_shape_or_features: 49 biomarkers (40 soluble + 9 cellular); 'soluble' subset = 40 soluble excl. Zym + TotalCellCount
datasets.notes: PERIT-PD cohort, University Hospital of Wales, 82 PD patients with acute peritonitis; 82 samples in this task. Classes: no growth, Gram-negative, streptococcal, CNS, other Gram-positive. Anonymised data released by authors at the repo; missing values imputed with MICE (RF).
datasets.split_as_reported: stratified 5-fold cross-validation; within each fold 80% train / 20% validation, RandomOverSampler applied inside training folds
datasets.booleanization: equal-width binning of each biomarker's [min,max] range into 2/3/4 intervals, one-hot encoded (4 ranges x 49 biomarkers = 196 bits)

extraction_notes: Filename says 2024 but published 2025 (accepted June 2025). Very small clinical cohort (82 patients) - 5-fold CV with high variance. Hierarchical steps modelled as separate dataset_ids (subsets of the same cohort). Table 2 TM/ANN accuracies are on the soluble biomarker subset; Table 3 uses 4 ranges (paper wording implies same soluble subset). Train P/R/F1 from Table 3 omitted except where noted. Table 4 (minimal biomarker counts per target accuracy) not encoded as results. ANN binary-step results come from Table 2 (Supplementary Table S6 not available).
